triage.intro: Pick what your system is doing. You’ll see the usual causes, what’s safe to check yourself, and what a fix typically costs.

urgencyLabels.soon: Book within a day or two

symptoms.label: Blowing warm air
symptoms.urgencyNote: When it’s over 100° outside, a house without cooling gets dangerous within hours, especially for older people, babies, and pets.
causes: Failed capacitor, the most common summer repair
Clogged filter starving the indoor coil of air
Tripped breaker or blown fuse at the outdoor disconnect
Low refrigerant from a leak
tryFirst: Set the thermostat to COOL, and below the room temperature
Check the breaker labeled AC or condenser
Pull the filter. If you can’t see light through it, replace it

symptoms.label: Turns on and off every few minutes
symptoms.urgencyNote: Short cycling wears out the compressor, which is the most expensive part of the system.
causes: Dirty condenser coil overheating the system
Thermostat in direct sun or right next to a vent
Low refrigerant
A system too large for the house
tryFirst: Check whether sun hits the thermostat in the afternoon

symptoms.label: Ice on the copper lines
symptoms.urgencyNote: Running a frozen system can push liquid refrigerant into the compressor. Thaw it first.
causes: Restricted airflow from a clogged filter or closed vents
Low refrigerant
A failing blower motor
tryFirst: Set the system to OFF and the fan to ON for 2–4 hours to thaw
Replace the filter and open any closed vents
Don’t chip at the ice. The coil fins bend easily

symptoms.label: Making a new noise
symptoms.urgencyNote: A grinding or banging noise means turn it off now. A buzz or hum can usually wait a day.
causes: Buzzing: a capacitor or contactor on its way out
Squealing: blower motor bearings
Banging or grinding: a loose or broken part inside
tryFirst: Turn the system off if it grinds or bangs
Note whether it happens at startup, while running, or at shutdown

symptoms.label: Bill went up, house isn’t cooler
symptoms.urgencyNote: This isn’t an emergency, but every month you wait shows up on the next bill.
causes: Leaky ducts in the attic
Dirty outdoor coil
An aging system losing efficiency
A thermostat schedule working against you
tryFirst: With the power off, rinse the outdoor coil gently with a hose

symptoms.label: Won’t turn on at all
symptoms.urgencyNote: Most no-power calls turn out to be a cheap fix, but in summer it still means today.
causes: Dead thermostat batteries
Tripped breaker
Float switch shut the system off because the condensate drain is clogged
Blown low-voltage fuse on the control board
tryFirst: Check the breakers for the air handler and the outdoor unit
Look for standing water in the drain pan under the indoor unit

repairOrReplace.intro: A rule of thumb many technicians use: multiply the system’s age by the repair quote. If the result is over $5,000, get a replacement quote before you pay for the repair.
repairOrReplace.repairBody: The math favors fixing what you have. Ask for the old part back so you can see what failed.
repairOrReplace.replaceBody: Repair money starts going into a system near the end of its life. Compare a written replacement price before you decide.
repairOrReplace.r22Note: Systems installed before about 2010 usually run on R-22 refrigerant. It hasn’t been made since 2020, so recharging one gets more expensive every year.
repairOrReplace.disclaimer: This is a rule of thumb, not a quote. We’ll give you both prices in writing.
